- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 1.0) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for volatility.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes; cap forecast peak at 2–3% above immediate prior high.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show rising prices, model often overshoots; adjust downward by 1–2% in next forecast.
- Forecast horizon 30d often lags true trend by 1–2 days; if sentiment is trending upward, shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
